newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish PZU expects to pay PLN 300 mln for floods.
newsitem.headline: Polish PZU expects to pay PLN 300 mln for floods.

text.p: Insurer Powszechny Zaklad Ubespieczen SA estimates its payments stemming from Poland's floods will total about 300 million zlotys and its financial results will be affected, its vice-president said on Monday.
But Elzbieta Turkowska-Tyrluk told a news conference there would be no danger to the liquidity of PZU, Poland's biggest insurer.

"The value of all compensation payments will be in the area of 300 million zlotys," she said, adding that there were likely to be 100,000 claims and the costs of adminstering and settling them would probably be an extra 20 million zlotys.
"This is a large sum, but there is no danger as regards the liquidity of PZU. We are turning to our reserves, but there is no threat of a loss of liquidity," she said.
"If our reserves have to be used, then overall the financial result for the end of the 1997 may be somewhat worse than we have foreseen," Turkowska-Tyrluk said without giving details.
A PZU press release said that such large payments would definitely have a negative effect on the result and instead of the planned profit the company could record a loss.
In April this year PZU said its net profit for the first quarter of 1997 was 204.9 million zlotys. It reported a loss of 169.7 million zlotys at the end of 1996.
